questions.text:
A functional dependency [latex]F:X \rightarrow Y[/latex] is termed as a useful functional dependency if and only if it satisfies all the following three conditions:

[latex]X[/latex] is not the empty set. [latex]Y[/latex] is not the empty set. Intersection of [latex]X[/latex] and [latex]Y[/latex] is the empty set.

For a relation [latex]R[/latex] with 4 attributes, the total number of possible useful functional dependencies is ______
questions.solution:
X and Y must be non-empty and disjoint. Each of the 4 attributes goes to X, to Y, or to neither: [latex]3^4=81[/latex] ways.

Remove cases with X empty ([latex]2^4=16[/latex]) and Y empty ([latex]16[/latex]); add back both empty (1):
[latex]81-16-16+1=50[/latex]

Answer: 50

questions.text:
A processor with 16 general purpose registers uses a 32-bit instruction format. The
instruction format consists of an opcode field, an addressing mode field, two register
operand fields, and a 16-bit scalar field. If 8 addressing modes are to be supported,
the maximum number of unique opcodes possible for every addressing mode
is _________
questions.solution:
Divide the 32 bits among the fields:
- 16 registers [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 4 bits per register field, two fields = 8 bits
- 8 addressing modes [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 3 bits
- Scalar field = 16 bits

Opcode bits [latex]=32-8-3-16=5[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]2^5=32[/latex] opcodes.

Answer: 32

questions.text:
A non-pipelined instruction execution unit operating at 2 GHz takes an average of
6 cycles to execute an instruction of a program P. The unit is then redesigned to
operate on a 5-stage pipeline at 2 GHz. Assume that the ideal throughput of the
pipelined unit is 1 instruction per cycle. In the execution of program P,
20% instructions incur an average of 2 cycles stall due to data hazards and
20% instructions incur an average of 3 cycles stall due to control hazards. The
speedup (rounded off to one decimal place) obtained by the pipelined design over
the non-pipelined design is ________
questions.solution:
Non-pipelined: 6 cycles per instruction.
Pipelined CPI [latex]=1+0.2\times2+0.2\times3=1+0.4+0.6=2[/latex]

Same clock (2 GHz), so speedup [latex]=6/2=3.0[/latex]

Answer: 3

questions.text: The number of distinct minimum-weight spanning trees of the following graph is _______
questions.solution:
Use Kruskal's idea.

- All four weight-1 edges (a-b, a-f, c-d, d-e) form no cycle, so every MST contains them. Components: {a, b, f}, {c, d, e}, {g}.
- Now g must be joined to both components using weight-2 edges:
[latex]\quad[/latex]g to {a, b, f}: g-a, g-b, g-f [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 3 choices
[latex]\quad[/latex]g to {c, d, e}: g-c, g-d, g-e [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 3 choices
- Weight-3 edges are never needed.

Number of MSTs [latex]=3\times3=9[/latex] (each of weight 8).

Answer: 9

questions.text: The chromatic number of a graph is the minimum number of colours used in a proper colouring of the graph. The chromatic number of the following graph is _______
questions.solution:
Number the 8 vertices 1 to 8 around the octagon.

- The 8 outer sides join consecutive vertices (odd-even).
- Every inner line (the 2 vertical, 2 horizontal and 4 slanted lines) joins two vertices 3 steps apart around the octagon, which is again one odd and one even vertex.

So colour odd vertices with colour 1 and even vertices with colour 2: no edge has both ends the same colour. The graph is bipartite, and it has edges, so it needs at least 2 colours.

Answer: 2
